items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Claudio Roditi' only as part of a list of trumpet players ('Jon Faddis, Claudio Roditi. Roy Hargrove. Every night a different trumpet player.') and does not describe any personal interaction, relationship, or collaboration with him.

ctx.x: Jon Faddis, Claudio Roditi. Roy Hargrove. Every night a different trumpet player. And that album came out and it was called “To Dizzy With Love.” And I had such a ball playing with him. It was like the first time I’d played with him for any length of time since I met the dude, and I was just really turned on because I idolized him so much, I’d learned so much from him. And comping, and the other horn players, I’d do something and he’d turn around and look at me and smile and wink. And so when he died I was in…

stopped in his dressing room and said, “Dizzy, thanks for inviting me to do this week, it was really a treat for me.” And he looked at me and grabbed me and hugged me and said, “You’re finally doing it.” You don’t know how much that meant to me. Because he had showed me so much. And he said, “You’re doing it, just keep on.” That was the last thing he said to me. He said, “See you next time.” There wasn’t a next time. In fact that’s when he got ill, when he left New York then and he went out to the coast and I…
